chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from al-Mu'alla, from Ibn Jumhur, from Safwan, from Ibn Miskan, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah about the Imams, and he said: 'Whoever denies one of the living [Imams] has denied the dead [ones].'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as)
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: The Imams, specifically the twelve infallible leaders in Shia belief
key_terms.الْأَحْيَاءِ: The living ones, referring to the Imams alive at the time of the narration
key_terms.الْأَمْوَاتِ: The dead ones, referring to the Imams who have passed away

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between denying a living Imam and a dead Imam in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Ibn Miskan inquires about the nature of the Imamate, prompting Imam al-Sadiq (as) to affirm the indivisible continuity of the twelve Imams. The Imam’s statement that denying one of the living is tantamount to denying the deceased underscores the theological principle that the Imamate is a singular, unbroken chain of divine authority, where the status of each Imam is intrinsically linked to the others. This establishes the validity of the current Imam during the Minor and Major Gheebah as the same essential reality as his predecessors.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (5) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from al-Husayn bin Muhammad from al-Mu’alla from ibn Jumhoor from Safwan that ibn Miskan had said:
I asked Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) about the imams and he said: “Whoever denies one of the alive imams, has denied the dead ones.”
